title: CT-based clinical deep learning radiomics nomogram for preoperative differentiation of pyelocaliceal upper tract urothelial carcinoma and xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis
summary: A CT radiomics and deep-learning nomogram was evaluated to distinguish upper-tract urothelial carcinoma from xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis in 161 patients with pathology-confirmed diagnoses. On an internal random split, the combined model had validation AUC 0.930 versus 0.695 for a radiologist. External validation and clinical utility remain unestablished.
organization: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University; Guangxi Medical University; First People’s Hospital of Yulin

evidence.tested: In 161 patients with pathology-confirmed UTUC or XGP, a random 112/49 training/validation split was used. The clinical deep-learning radiomics model had validation AUC 0.930 and exceeded a radiologist’s AUC of 0.695 in this cohort.
evidence.unknown: The evidence is internal validation in a limited cohort; external validation and clinical utility are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Radiomics and deep-learning features from preoperative CT were combined to distinguish upper-tract urothelial carcinoma from xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
